content:
Hey.

Interestingly, this PR changed the notion of OFE to use strict equality, i.e.:

@[rocq_alias ofe]
class OFE (α : Type _) where
  -- Equiv : α → α → Prop  / removed
  Dist : Nat → α → α → Prop
  dist_eqv : Equivalence (Dist n)
  -- equiv_dist : Equiv x y ↔ ∀ n, Dist n x y / removed
  eq_dist : x = y ↔ ∀ n, Dist n x y
  dist_lt : Dist n x y → m < n → Dist m x y -- added

I have a model for the old version that would use a notion of 'equality up to validity' (let's call it bientail) - it is unfortunately now impossible to model this, because I can't prove that bientail x y -> x = y, for the invalid case.

Is the intent here to disallow such models on purpose?

We discuss this change in depth in the Iris-Lean paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24252v1. Indeed, UPred is also "up to validity" and there we found that subtyping was the right move in order to make equivalence coincide with equality. We also provide a generic quotient OFE for tricker cases.

Perhaps you could share your OFE? We are reasonably confident that most OFE's can fit into this framework.

Hi!
Our rationale is that in a setting with extensionality axioms + choice/quotients it is possible to do setoid-free iris. Perhaps, taking a look at changes to uPred that Markus has mentioned and a new definition of agreement algebra can be useful.
Would quotienting by bientail and moving validity from the relation to the data help in your usecase?

This works just fine indeed, I am not sure how this solution eluded me.
Appreciate the help.

Also thank you so much for everyone's hard work on Iris-Lean, it's been surprisingly pleasant to work with.
